entries.definition: The balance sheet is a ‘snapshot’ of an organization’s assets and liabilities on a particular date. The balance sheet shows the sources of funds provided to an organization (called the capital employed and normally either equity or debt) and how those funds have been used by the organization to invest in fixed assets (assets the organization intends to keep for more than one year) and working capital (money tied up in the day to day operations of the business).

entries.definition: Book value is the accounting carrying amount (historical cost less depreciation); market value is what the asset or equity trades for.

entries.definition: There are two types of stock - common stock and preferred stock. Most shares tend to be common stock and generally carry one vote each and carry an equal right to a proportionate share of dividends. Capital stock is not a liability in the sense of other sources of funds (e.g. bank loans) since it is not generally paid back to shareholders unless the company is wound up.

entries.definition: Most shares tend to be common stock carrying one vote each and with an equal right to a proportionate share of dividends. Common stock dividends tend to rise as profits grow. This is in contrast to preferred stock where the dividend tends to be fixed.

entries.definition: Ratios that analyze a company’s liquidity or its ability to “cover” its financial debt obligations. An example of a coverage ratio is EBITDA / Interest expense.

entries.definition: See accounts payable.

entries.definition: Current assets are all assets other than fixed assets. They are either cash or assets expected to be converted into cash or consumed in the business during the year. Current assets include items such as cash, accounts receivable and inventory.
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: An organization’s liabilities due within one year. Current liabilities include items such as short term loans, any element of long term loans due within one year, and accounts payable.
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: Current assets / current liabilities. This ratio measures short term liquidity, whether or not a company will have the ability to cover its obligations in the short term.
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: Current assets/liabilities are expected to convert to cash or be settled within one year (or the operating cycle); everything else is non-current.
entries.how_to_evaluate: Current ratio and quick ratio measure the cover of current liabilities by current assets.
entries.source: PwC deck

entries.definition: Used to test one or two variables for sensitivity analysis.
entries.source: CFI Financial Modeling Fundamentals Glossary (PDF)

entries.definition: Average days inventory is held.
entries.gaap_vs_ifrs: LIFO (US GAAP only) lowers inventory and raises COGS in inflation, distorting DIO versus IFRS peers; use the LIFO reserve to restate.
entries.source: authored

entries.definition: Average days taken to pay suppliers.
entries.how_to_evaluate: Cash conversion cycle = DSO + DIO − DPO.
entries.source: authored

entries.definition: Average days to collect receivables.
entries.how_to_evaluate: Rising DSO with flat revenue flags collection problems or channel stuffing.
entries.source: authored

entries.definition: Discounted cash flow analysis. A financial evaluation method that takes the “time value of money” into account.
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: Capital used to finance an organization that is subject to payment of interest over the life of the loan, at the end of which the loan is normally repaid.
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: Raising money for a business through loans or by issuing bonds.

entries.definition: See accounts receivable.

entries.definition: Tax payable in future periods because book profit is recognised before taxable profit (e.g. accelerated tax depreciation, asset write-ups in an acquisition).
entries.formula: New DTL in a deal = (PP&E + intangible write-ups) × tax rate
entries.gaap_vs_ifrs: Both use the balance-sheet liability method; IFRS (IAS 12) classifies all deferred taxes as non-current and requires 'probable' recognition of deferred tax assets, US GAAP recognises DTAs in full with a valuation allowance.
entries.source: authored

entries.definition: Systematic allocation of the cost of tangible fixed assets over their useful lives (straight-line, declining balance, units of production).
entries.gaap_vs_ifrs: IFRS (IAS 16) requires component depreciation and allows the revaluation model; US GAAP uses historical cost only and component depreciation is permitted but rare. Impairment reversals are allowed under IFRS (IAS 36), prohibited under US GAAP.
entries.how_to_evaluate: Depreciation waves per capex vintage in the LBO; % of opening PP&E in the CFI models.
entries.toolkit: three_statement PPE schedule; lbo depreciation_detail; xlcalc SLN/SYD
entries.source: authored
entries.alt_definition: Depreciation of fixed assets is the process of allocating part of the cost of fixed assets to a particular accounting period. Depreciation is normally charged to the income statement on a straight line basis (although there are alternative methods available). For example, if a car is bought for $15,000, has an expected life of 5 years, and has a residual value (expected scrap value) of $5,000, then the depreciation expense in the income statement will be $2,000 per year for 5 years. The value of the car in the balance sheet would start at $15,000 but would be reduced by $2,000 a year. At the end of year 1 the net book value (NBV) of the car in the balance sheet would be $13,000. At the end of year 2, the NBV would be $11,000. The accumulated depreciation for the car at the end of year 2 would be $4,000.

entries.definition: Direct costs are those that are directly attributable to the product or service provided by the organization. They are included in cost of goods sold.
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: A share of a company’s net profits distributed by the company to a class of its stockholders.
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: Decomposes return on equity into margin, asset turnover and leverage.
entries.how_to_evaluate: Separates operating performance from financial gearing.
entries.source: authored

entries.definition: Net income attributable to common shareholders divided by weighted-average shares; diluted EPS adds in-the-money options, warrants and convertibles (treasury stock method).
entries.gaap_vs_ifrs: IAS 33 and ASC 260 are largely converged; minor differences in contracts settleable in cash or shares and in year-to-date diluted share calculations.
entries.toolkit: merger.deal['combined']['eps']; CFI Treasury Stock Method calculator

entries.definition: Earnings before interest and taxes (operating income).
entries.how_to_evaluate: Base for NOPAT = EBIT × (1 − t) and unlevered FCF.
entries.source: authored
entries.alt_definition: Earnings before interest and taxes. See operating profit.

entries.definition: EBIT / Sales.
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation: operating profit plus non-cash D&A, a proxy for operating cash generation used in leverage multiples and enterprise-value multiples.
entries.gaap_vs_ifrs: IFRS 16 puts all leases on balance sheet so lease costs become depreciation + interest and EBITDA rises; under US GAAP operating leases keep a straight-line lease expense inside EBITDA. Add back lease expense (EBITDAR) or capitalise consistently before comparing.
entries.how_to_evaluate: Never compare EBITDA multiples across IFRS and US GAAP lessees without a lease adjustment.
entries.toolkit: three_statement, lbo (tranche sizing = multiple × EBITDA), dcf terminal multiple
entries.source: authored
entries.alt_definition: Earnings before interest, taxation, depreciation, and amortization.

entries.definition: Value of the operating business to all capital providers: market equity value plus debt, preferred and non-controlling interests, minus cash.
entries.formula: Equity value + debt + preferred + NCI − cash
entries.gaap_vs_ifrs: Under IFRS 16 lease liabilities are debt-like for every lessee; under US GAAP operating-lease liabilities are also recognised (ASC 842) but presented separately — decide consistently whether to include them in EV.
entries.how_to_evaluate: Pair EV with unlevered metrics (EBITDA, EBIT, revenue) only.
entries.source: authored

entries.definition: Total assets less total liabilities. Also called shareholders’ equity, net worth or book value.
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: The money acquired from the business owners themselves or from other investors.
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: Value attributable to shareholders: EV + cash − debt, or price × diluted shares.
entries.how_to_evaluate: Pair with levered metrics (net income, book equity).
entries.source: authored

entries.definition: Number of acquirer shares issued per target share in a stock deal.
entries.formula: Offer price per target share / acquirer share price
entries.how_to_evaluate: Fixed vs floating exchange ratios shift price risk between the parties.
entries.source: authored

entries.definition: EV/EBITDA multiple assumed at sale; usually set equal to (or below) the entry multiple to avoid banking on multiple expansion.
entries.how_to_evaluate: Sensitise IRR to exit multiple × operating scenario (the data table).
entries.source: authored

entries.definition: One-off gains or losses outside normal operations.
entries.gaap_vs_ifrs: IFRS prohibits the 'extraordinary' label; US GAAP eliminated it in 2015 (ASU 2015-01). Both require separate disclosure of unusual items.
entries.how_to_evaluate: Normalise EBIT/EBITDA by removing them before applying multiples.
entries.source: authored

entries.definition: The promises made by the borrowing firm in a loan agreement to adhere to certain limits in the firm’s operations.
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: A mathematical model describing the interrelationships among various financial variables. Typically financial models are broken down into inputs, processing, and outputs.
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: Statements, in financial terms, of the financial position of an entity at a given date, or of the results of its operations for a given period. The statements are normally prepared in one of a number of standard formats. Most commonly, when people refer to financial statements, they mean the income statement, the balance sheet, the cash flow statement and the related notes to the accounts.
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: Assets intended for use on a continuing basis in an organization’s activities (normally defined as assets an organization intends to keep for more than one year). There are three categories of fixed assets: intangible, tangible and investments.
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: Coverage of interest plus lease/rent and scheduled principal by EBITDA (or EBIT) plus fixed charges.
entries.how_to_evaluate: Common LBO covenant.
entries.toolkit: CFI Fixed Charge Coverage template; BIWS FCCR example
entries.source: authored

entries.definition: Chart of valuation ranges by method (DCF, comps, precedents, LBO) against the current price.
entries.how_to_evaluate: The standard one-page valuation summary.
entries.toolkit: charts.range_bars; CFI Football Field Chart template
entries.source: authored

entries.definition: The projection or estimate of future sales, revenue, earnings, or costs.
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: Cash available to shareholders after debt service: net income + D&A − capex − ΔNWC + net borrowing.
entries.formula: NI + D&A − capex − ΔNWC + net debt issued
entries.how_to_evaluate: Discount at the cost of equity; used for financials and highly levered firms.
entries.source: authored

entries.definition: Used to test which assumptions are needed to satisfy the desired output.
entries.source: CFI Financial Modeling Fundamentals Glossary (PDF)

entries.definition: Excess of purchase price over the fair value of identifiable net assets acquired; not amortised, tested for impairment.
entries.formula: Purchase equity value − FV of net identifiable assets (after write-ups and deferred taxes)
entries.gaap_vs_ifrs: Both prohibit amortisation and require impairment testing; IFRS (IAS 36) tests at the cash-generating unit with a one-step recoverable-amount test, US GAAP (ASC 350) at the reporting unit with an optional qualitative screen and a one-step quantitative test. Neither allows reversal of goodwill impairment. US private companies may elect amortisation.
entries.how_to_evaluate: Compare goodwill to equity; a large impairment signals an overpaid deal.
entries.toolkit: merger.pro_forma purchase_price_allocation; lbo closing balance sheet
entries.source: authored
entries.alt_definition: When one company buys another company it typically pays more than the book value of the net assets acquired (because it is acquiring staff, name / reputation, and customer relationships). This excess of the purchase price over the fair book value of the net assets is called goodwill. Goodwill is normally included in the balance sheet as an intangible fixed asset.

entries.definition: Gross profit / Sales revenue. Gross margin shows how much was spent producing the good or service that was sold for every dollar of sales revenue.
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: Sales revenue less cost of sales.
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: Write-down of an asset's carrying amount to its recoverable amount when it can no longer be supported.
entries.gaap_vs_ifrs: IFRS: one-step test against recoverable amount (higher of value in use and fair value less costs of disposal), reversals permitted except goodwill. US GAAP: two-step for long-lived assets (undiscounted recoverability screen, then fair value), no reversals.
entries.how_to_evaluate: Treat as non-cash; adjust EBITDA and normalise earnings.
entries.source: authored

entries.definition: earnings The income statement is an organization’s ‘financial history book’ and summarizes the revenue, expenses and operating profit for the financial year. It also shows the tax charged against profit, how much of the profit for the year has been paid out in dividends and how much has been retained in the business.
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: Financial model assumptions that are used to drive model outputs.
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: Intangible fixed assets have no ‘physical’ presence. Examples include patents, goodwill, trademarks and brand names.
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: These are liabilities that bear interest, normally short term borrowings. They are excluded from some ratios in order to factor in the cost of financing.
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: EBITDA / Interest expense. This solvency ratio shows how much income is available to service debt costs.
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: Ability to service interest from operating profit.
entries.formula: EBIT / interest expense (or EBITDA / cash interest)
entries.gaap_vs_ifrs: Lease reclassification under IFRS 16 raises EBIT and interest simultaneously — recompute on a like-for-like basis.
entries.how_to_evaluate: Damodaran maps coverage to a synthetic rating and default spread.
entries.source: authored

entries.definition: Discount rate at which NPV is zero; XIRR uses dated flows.
entries.how_to_evaluate: Needs at least one sign change; compare with WACC (projects) or the sponsor hurdle (LBO).
entries.source: authored

entries.definition: Inventory normally refers to items held for resale and may include raw materials, work in progress and finished goods.
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: Inventories / COGS x 365. Average number of days goods remain in inventory before being sold.
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: Sales / Inventory (either the ending balance, or average inventory balance). This ratio illustrates how a company manages its inventory.
entries.formula: Sales / Inventory (either the ending balance, or average inventory balance)
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: Cost flow assumption for inventory: FIFO, weighted average or LIFO.
entries.gaap_vs_ifrs: LIFO is allowed under US GAAP and prohibited by IFRS (IAS 2); IFRS measures at lower of cost and net realisable value with reversals allowed, US GAAP at lower of cost and NRV (non-LIFO) or market (LIFO) with no reversals.
entries.how_to_evaluate: Add the LIFO reserve to inventory and subtract its change from COGS to restate a LIFO filer to FIFO.
entries.source: authored

entries.definition: Deals or transactions involving sale or purchase of equipment, plant, properties, securities, or other assets.
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: Direct labour / Sales. Cost of goods sold is made up of labour, materials, and direct costs. This margin shows the proportion of labour that goes to make up each dollar of sales.
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: Sales / Land and buildings. The sales generated from land and buildings is measured by this ratio.
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: Right-of-use asset and lease liability recognised for most leases.
entries.gaap_vs_ifrs: IFRS 16 has a single lessee model (all leases financing-type: depreciation + interest). ASC 842 keeps operating leases with a single straight-line lease cost in operating expenses. Effect: IFRS EBITDA, operating cash flow and debt are all higher than for an identical US GAAP company.
entries.how_to_evaluate: Add lease liabilities to net debt and use EBITDAR, or de-capitalise, before comparing.
entries.source: authored

entries.definition: Ratios that analyze a company’s solvency or the level of its debt financing relative to its equity financing. An example of a leverage ratio is Total debt / Total shareholders’ equity.
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: Acquisition funded mostly with debt secured on the target's cash flows; the sponsor's return comes from EBITDA growth, multiple expansion and debt paydown.

entries.source: authored

entries.definition: Money owed, or other financial obligations to other organizations Liabilities and individuals.
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: See debt.
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: Materials / Sales. Cost of goods sold is made up of labour, materials, and direct costs. This margin shows the proportion of materials that goes to make up each dollar of sales.
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: Debt ranking below senior loans, priced with higher coupons, often PIK-able, and frequently carrying equity warrants.

entries.definition: The framework around which a financial model is built.
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: Total cash returned divided by cash invested, ignoring timing.
entries.how_to_evaluate: Read together with IRR: a 2x over 3 years is ~26% IRR, over 7 years ~10%.

entries.definition: By naming a cell, you use the name reference rather than the cell reference.

entries.definition: A complicated formula with multiple IF statements within each other.
entries.source: CFI Financial Modeling Fundamentals Glossary (PDF)

entries.definition: Sales / Net assets. This ratio takes into account the financing of assets, and measures management’s efficiency in relation to the use of assets.
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: Total assets less total liabilities.
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: Net book value typically refers to property plant and equipment (PP&E). The net book value of PP&E is calculated by taking the total gross cost of PP&E and deducting total accumulated depreciation / amortization.

entries.definition: Total debt less cash and cash equivalents.
entries.how_to_evaluate: Net debt / EBITDA is the standard leverage multiple; covenants usually cap it.
entries.source: authored

entries.definition: for the year The profits retained by an organization after all expenses including interest expenses, taxes and dividends. The retained profits / earnings for a given year are reinvested in the business (hopefully making the organization grow, and increasing the value of its shares) and are added to ‘retained earnings’ in the balance sheet (which represent all retained profits accumulated over an organization’s entire life to date which have been reinvested in the business).
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: See net earnings.
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: Sum of cash flows discounted to today; XNPV discounts by actual dates (days/365) rather than whole periods.
entries.formula: NPV = Σ CF_t / (1 + r)^t; XNPV = Σ CF_i / (1 + r)^((d_i − d_0)/365)
entries.how_to_evaluate: Excel NPV discounts the first flow one full period — put the time-0 flow outside NPV().
entries.source: authored

entries.definition: Net income / Sales. This margin shows how much is earned for every dollar of sales revenue.
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: Operating current assets less operating current liabilities (typically receivables + inventory + prepaids − payables − accruals), excluding cash and debt.
entries.formula: AR + inventory + prepaids − AP − accrued expenses
entries.gaap_vs_ifrs: Inventory: LIFO permitted under US GAAP, prohibited under IFRS (IAS 2); write-downs to NRV can be reversed under IFRS, not under US GAAP.
entries.how_to_evaluate: Model with days assumptions; an increase in NWC consumes cash.

entries.definition: Assets that are not expected to be converted into cash within 12 months of the balance sheet date.
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: before interest and income taxes (PBIT) Cash inflows and outflows relating to a company’s operations. Examples includes receiving payments from customers, paying salaries, etc.
synonyms: earnings before interest and income taxes (EBIT)
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: Assets acquired for or used throughout the operations of the business (such as cash, inventory, prepaid expenses, equipment).
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: Operating costs / Sales. This margin shows the operating expenses as a percentage of sales. This does not include cost of goods sold (as is the case with the operating profit margin), so is an indication of the efficiency of the operation.
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: before interest and income taxes (PBIT) Sales revenues less all operating expenses. Operating profit is calculated before financing costs and taxes. It is often referred to as EBIT.
synonyms: earnings before interest and income taxes (EBIT)
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: Otherwise known as the EBIT margin. Operating income / Sales. This performance ratio shows the cost of running the operation for each dollar of sales.
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: The net sales revenue accumulated by a firm.
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: See common stock.
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: Financial model calculations that are driven by one or more inputs.
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: Interest accrued to the principal instead of paid in cash, common on mezzanine/subordinated debt.
entries.formula: PIK accrual = opening balance × rate × PIK share
entries.gaap_vs_ifrs: Deductibility of PIK interest for tax differs by jurisdiction; both GAAP and IFRS accrue it as interest expense.
entries.how_to_evaluate: Non-cash: add back in cash flow; the balance compounds.
entries.source: authored

entries.definition: Personnel costs / Sales. The personnel costs used in this ratio could be research and development specific, or general overhead personnel costs, or total personnel depending upon the type of organization. This margin is useful in monitoring the amount spent on wages, salaries, and related expenses for each dollar of sales.
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: Sales / Plant and Machinery. This ratio measures the efficiency of the company’s operating assets.
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: Multiples paid in past M&A deals for similar companies, including control premia.
entries.formula: Implied EV = precedent multiple × target metric
entries.how_to_evaluate: Usually higher than trading comps because of the premium; check deal timing and cycle.
entries.source: authored

entries.definition: Preferred stock has preferential rights over common stock to both dividends and also to assets in the event that a company is wound up (i.e. preferred stock holders are paid out before common stock holders). Typically preferred stock dividends are fixed (e.g. 6 percent preferred stock) and do not increase with rising profits.
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: The translation of financial model inputs or assumptions into financial model outputs.
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: Non-current fixed or capital assets such as buildings, computers, land, and vehicles.
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.term: Property, Plant And Equipment (Pp&E) Turnover Ratio
entries.definition: Sales / Property, Plant & Equipment. This ratio measures the sales a company is able to generate from capital assets.
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: Allocating the purchase price to acquired assets and liabilities at fair value (PP&E and intangibles write-ups, new deferred tax liability), with the residual as goodwill.
entries.formula: Goodwill = price − book value + old goodwill − write-ups − DTL written down + new DTL
entries.gaap_vs_ifrs: IFRS 3 and ASC 805 are largely converged; differences remain on NCI measurement (IFRS allows proportionate share; US GAAP requires full fair value) and contingent liabilities.
entries.how_to_evaluate: Write-ups create extra D&A that depresses reported EPS; show 'adjusted' EPS excluding it.
entries.source: authored

entries.definition: Current assets - Inventory / Current liabilities. This ratio provides a more prudent measure of short-term liquidity recognizing the inventory can not always be readily converted into cash.
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: When copied across multiple cells, they change based on the relative position of rows and columns.
entries.source: CFI Financial Modeling Fundamentals Glossary (PDF)

entries.definition: Research and development costs / Sales. This margin shows how much the company invests in developing the next generation of products or services for each dollar of sales.
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: These expenses are directly attributable to researching and developing new or improved products or systems.
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: Reserves are part of shareholders’ equity. Reserves are subdivided into revenue reserves (e.g. retained earnings), which are available to be distributed to the shareholders by way of dividends, and capital reserves (e.g. contributed surplus), which for various reasons are not distributable as dividends.
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: Retained earnings in the balance sheet represent all retained profits accumulated over an organization’s entire life to date which have been reinvested in the business. As the retained earnings ultimately belong to shareholders, they are included as part of shareholders’ equity.
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: See net earnings.
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: After-tax operating profit relative to the capital invested in operations.
entries.how_to_evaluate: Value is created when ROIC exceeds WACC (Koller); in an LBO the BIWS sweep model tracks ROIC yearly.
entries.source: authored

entries.definition: Revenue includes both cash sales and credit sales of goods and services, but does not include the sale of fixed assets.
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: Five-step model: identify the contract, performance obligations, transaction price, allocation, and recognise when control transfers.
entries.gaap_vs_ifrs: Converged standards; remaining differences are in collectability thresholds, licence renewals and some cost capitalisation.
entries.how_to_evaluate: Check deferred revenue and contract assets when revenue growth outpaces cash.
entries.source: authored

entries.definition: Committed line of credit drawn when cash falls below the minimum balance and repaid from surplus cash.
entries.formula: Draw = max(0, prior balance − cash available)
entries.how_to_evaluate: Interest on the revolver is circular with cash; the ASM template leaves it out, this toolkit can iterate it.
entries.source: authored

entries.definition: See revenue.
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: Running the model under alternative coherent input sets (base / upside / downside) selected by a switch (CHOOSE / INDEX).
entries.how_to_evaluate: Keep scenario inputs in one block; drive with a single selector cell.
entries.source: authored

entries.definition: Used to test for different scenarios that may happen in the future, usually base, worst and best.
entries.source: CFI Financial Modeling Fundamentals Glossary (PDF)

entries.definition: Tests the model’s robustness against possible future changes.
entries.source: CFI Financial Modeling Fundamentals Glossary (PDF)

entries.definition: Selling costs / Sales. This margin shows how much it costs to sell each dollar of sales.
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: Tests the final value against changes in one (or more) variables.
entries.source: CFI Financial Modeling Fundamentals Glossary (PDF)

entries.definition: Recomputing an output over a grid of one or two inputs (Excel Data Table); a heatmap is the natural visual.
entries.how_to_evaluate: Use for WACC × g (DCF), scenario × exit multiple (LBO), premium × % stock (merger).
entries.source: authored

entries.definition: Operational expenses that include direct and indirect selling expenses and all general and administrative expenses. Rent, heat, lights are all examples of general expenses.
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: See capital stock.
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: See contributed surplus.
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: See equity.
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: See capital stock.
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: Used to minimize or maximize the output under a certain set of assumptions.
entries.source: CFI Financial Modeling Fundamentals Glossary (PDF)

entries.definition: Funding table for a transaction: where the money comes from (equity, each debt tranche, cash on hand) and what it pays for (equity purchase, debt refinanced, fees).
entries.how_to_evaluate: Fees are capitalised (financing) or expensed (transaction) and flow through the closing balance sheet.
entries.source: authored

entries.definition: See income statement.
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: See capital stock.
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: When a corporation buys back its own shares in the open market.
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: Incremental value from combining businesses: cost synergies (overhead, procurement) and revenue synergies (cross-selling, pricing), phased in by a realisation schedule and offset by integration costs.
entries.formula: Value of synergies = PV of after-tax synergy cash flows − integration costs
entries.how_to_evaluate: Cost synergies are credited more than revenue synergies; pre-tax break-even synergies = dilution ÷ (1 − t) × shares.
entries.source: authored

entries.definition: Tangible fixed assets are fixed assets that have physical presence and include things like land, buildings, machinery, equipment, computers and so on.
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: The tax liability that companies, and individuals, are required to pay by law.
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: Tax / Sales. This efficiency ratio shows how well management is managing tax.
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: Value of cash flows beyond the explicit forecast, by perpetuity growth (Gordon) or an exit multiple.
entries.formula: TV = FCF_n × (1 + g) / (WACC − g); or multiple × EBITDA_n
entries.how_to_evaluate: Cross-check the implied exit multiple of the perpetuity method and the implied growth of the multiple method.
entries.source: authored

entries.definition: Inputting specific test data to stress test and sanity test your model. www.corporatefinanceinstitute.com
entries.source: CFI Financial Modeling Fundamentals Glossary (PDF)

entries.definition: www.corporatefinanceinstitute.com Shows the cells that use the selected cell in its calculations.
entries.source: CFI Financial Modeling Fundamentals Glossary (PDF)

entries.definition: Shows the cells that are used in the calculation of the selected cell.
entries.source: CFI Financial Modeling Fundamentals Glossary (PDF)

entries.definition: Valuation from multiples of similar listed companies (EV/EBITDA, EV/revenue, P/E), applied to the target's metrics.
entries.formula: Implied EV = peer median multiple × target metric
entries.gaap_vs_ifrs: Use consistent accounting (lease, LIFO, development-cost adjustments) across the peer set.
entries.how_to_evaluate: Report the 25th–75th percentile range in the football field.
entries.toolkit: BIWS comps files in catalog; charts.range_bars
entries.source: authored

entries.definition: Counts options and warrants in diluted shares net of shares repurchasable with the exercise proceeds.
entries.formula: Net new shares = options − (options × strike / price)
entries.source: authored

entries.definition: See revenue.
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: Ratios that measure an assets’ activity or efficiency in generating revenues or cash. Total assets / Sales.
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: Cash available to all capital providers before financing: NOPAT plus D&A less capex and the increase in net working capital.
entries.gaap_vs_ifrs: Lease classification (IFRS 16 vs ASC 842) and capitalised development costs (IAS 38 allows capitalisation of development spend; US GAAP expenses most R&D) shift items between opex and capex — FCF should be similar but EBITDA and capex lines are not comparable.
entries.how_to_evaluate: Discount at WACC; reconcile to CFO − capex.
entries.source: authored

entries.definition: One of the lookup and reference functions, is used to find things in a table or a range by row.
entries.source: CFI Financial Modeling Fundamentals Glossary (PDF)

entries.definition: Bridge from a starting value through positive and negative steps to an ending value (cash bridge, EV → equity bridge, returns attribution, PPA).
entries.source: authored

entries.definition: Blended after-tax return required by debt and equity investors, used to discount unlevered cash flows.
entries.how_to_evaluate: k_e from CAPM: r_f + β × ERP (+ country / size premia); k_d from yield or synthetic rating.
entries.toolkit: dcf.discount_rate; Damodaran wacccalc.xls; CFI WACC Calculator
entries.source: authored

entries.definition: Direct overhead / Sales. Cost of goods sold is made up of labour, materials, and direct costs. This margin shows the proportion of direct overhead that goes to make up each dollar of sales.
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: Working capital is normally defined as money tied up in the day to day operations of an organization. It is approximately equal to current assets less current liabilities. However, many analysts will define working capital more explicitly as inventory and accounts receivable less accounts payable (and exclude other current assets / liabilities such as cash and non-trade receivables and payables).
entries.source: CFI Financial Analysis Glossary (PDF on your CFI dashboard)

entries.definition: Fraction of a year between two dates; Excel's default basis 0 is US 30/360, used to scale a partial first forecast period in a DCF.
entries.how_to_evaluate: The CFI DCF stub 31-Dec-2017 → 30-Jun-2018 is exactly 0.5.
entries.source: authored

gaap_vs_ifrs.how_to_evaluate: Expect more policy choices under IFRS; read the accounting-policies note first.

gaap_vs_ifrs.ifrs: Usually non-current first; liquidity order permitted

gaap_vs_ifrs.us_gaap: LIFO allowed; lower of cost or NRV/market; no reversal of write-downs
gaap_vs_ifrs.ifrs: LIFO prohibited (IAS 2); lower of cost and NRV; reversals allowed
gaap_vs_ifrs.how_to_evaluate: Restate LIFO to FIFO using the LIFO reserve; DIO and gross margin otherwise not comparable.
Revalued assets inflate equity and depreciation; adjust P/B and ROE.

gaap_vs_ifrs.ifrs: Required when components have different lives
gaap_vs_ifrs.how_to_evaluate: Depreciation profiles differ; use EBITDA or cash capex for comparisons.

gaap_vs_ifrs.ifrs: Capitalised when IAS 38 criteria are met
gaap_vs_ifrs.how_to_evaluate: IFRS EBITDA and capex are higher; add back capitalised development to compare R&D intensity.

gaap_vs_ifrs.us_gaap: Two-step (undiscounted recoverability, then fair value); no reversals
gaap_vs_ifrs.ifrs: One-step to recoverable amount; reversals allowed (not goodwill)
gaap_vs_ifrs.how_to_evaluate: IFRS earnings can bounce back after reversals; normalise.

gaap_vs_ifrs.us_gaap: Impairment only; optional qualitative screen; reporting-unit level; private-company amortisation election
gaap_vs_ifrs.ifrs: Impairment only at CGU level; annual test
gaap_vs_ifrs.how_to_evaluate: Neither amortises; impairments are non-cash — exclude from EBITDA.

gaap_vs_ifrs.us_gaap: ASC 842: operating leases keep straight-line lease cost in opex
gaap_vs_ifrs.ifrs: IFRS 16: all leases on balance sheet as depreciation + interest
gaap_vs_ifrs.how_to_evaluate: IFRS EBITDA, CFO and net debt are higher; use EBITDAR or add lease liabilities to EV for both.

gaap_vs_ifrs.us_gaap: Interest paid/received and dividends received = operating; dividends paid = financing
gaap_vs_ifrs.ifrs: Policy choice: interest paid operating or financing; dividends received operating or investing
gaap_vs_ifrs.how_to_evaluate: Normalise interest into a single bucket before computing FCF.

gaap_vs_ifrs.us_gaap: DTAs in full with valuation allowance; current/non-current split historically, now non-current
gaap_vs_ifrs.how_to_evaluate: Effective tax rate reconciliation is the check.

gaap_vs_ifrs.us_gaap: CECL (lifetime expected losses at inception) for credit losses
gaap_vs_ifrs.how_to_evaluate: Provisioning timing differs; matters for banks and receivables-heavy models.

gaap_vs_ifrs.ifrs: Split into liability and equity components (IAS 32)
gaap_vs_ifrs.how_to_evaluate: Interest expense and diluted EPS differ.
Largely comparable; watch collectability threshold and licence renewals.

gaap_vs_ifrs.us_gaap: ASC 805; NCI at full fair value
gaap_vs_ifrs.ifrs: IFRS 3; NCI at fair value or proportionate share
gaap_vs_ifrs.how_to_evaluate: Goodwill differs by the NCI choice under IFRS.

gaap_vs_ifrs.us_gaap: ASC 718; graded vesting may use straight-line
gaap_vs_ifrs.ifrs: IFRS 2; graded vesting requires accelerated attribution

gaap_vs_ifrs.how_to_evaluate: Quarterly margins are smoother under US GAAP.
Rebuild COGS vs opex lines when a by-nature IFRS statement is compared with US peers.
